correctness.rationale: Independence of directed arcs yields multinomial histogram covariance within the in- and out-degree classes. A single shared directed arc when heads/tails differ gives exactly n(n-1)p(1-p) times a difference-binomial rank-one kernel. Standardized binomial score v and constant u are orthonormal, yielding three zero eigenvectors, one 2n eigenvector, and all other eigenvalues n. Exact fractions checked for n=2,3,4 and p=1/3,2/3 in extracted verify.py; no finite experiment substituted for the all-n proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Full-text models and principal results were compared. A configuration model or preferential-attachment CLT does not imply an exact finite covariance for all independent-arc directed graphs; the older undirected asymptotic approximation likewise gives no exact paired directed histogram spectrum.

originality.rationale: The comparison objects genuinely differ: Chen–Olvera-Cravioto use prescribed degree distributions with a configuration model; Wang–Resnick use a directed preferential attachment process and a bidegree-pair count martingale CLT; McKay–Wormald study undirected degree-sequence approximations. Tournament-style two-way match outcomes are mutually exclusive and therefore do not encode the present independent-arc paired degree histograms. Explicit paired directed-degree covariance spectrum and contrast expectation were not found in searched materials, though implicit Bernoulli-matrix historical coverage remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unlocated older Bernoulli random-matrix row/column occupancy theorem may algebraically imply the exact covariance spectrum.
Complete McKay–Wormald 1997 full text was not inspected; the degree-sequence model differs, but exhaustive historical exclusion is unavailable.
Literature search cannot establish uniqueness, and unpublished work is not covered.

value.rationale: Directed-network empirical in- and out-degree histograms are natural goodness-of-fit summaries. A complete finite covariance decomposition is more informative than a single cell covariance: it identifies three exact constraints, a universal doubled eigenmode, all residual eigenspaces, and the exact n-2 calibration of a natural Pearson in/out discrepancy. These structural facts distinguish paired directed histograms from ordinary separate multinomial samples; the invariant is not an arbitrary small parameter slice.
